title: Acceptance Sentinel: PRD and Cutover Checklist for Hosted Chat/Embed/Rerank Endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objectives: Produce a compact PRD and an operational cutover checklist that guarantees deterministic behavior and safe rollouts for the hosted inference surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). This ticket scopes the behavioral contracts, canary plan, rollback triggers, QA acceptance, and monitoring playbook needed to launch or change endpoint behavior with minimal customer disruption. Motivation: recurring post-launch regressions in generation quality and knee-jerk infra rollbacks have caused customer impact and longer incident MTTR. We want a repeatable pre-launch sentinel that ties evals, telemetry, and runbook automation into go/no-go gates.
scope: In-scope: API behavioral contracts for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank; deterministic fallback policies; canary traffic slices and metrics; pre-launch QA harness (benchmarks + accept/reject criteria); console ops runbook with automated rollback hooks; per-route telemetry dashboards and alerts; documentation for customers on behavior changes. Out-of-scope: Dedicated capacity SLA re-pricing; on-prem installer changes; model architecture or training adjustments.
non_goals: Do not include changes to billing or quotas, large-scale model swaps outside compatible variants, or migration of the Dedicated product line. This PRD does not rework core serving kernels or quantization defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Contract: JSON schema for endpoint request/response fields validated and backward-compatible across minor versions
Behavioral: For each lane, defined determinism tolerances (random seed variance, sampling ranges) and a signed-off eval suite with pass/fail thresholds
Latency: 95th p99 tail latency within SLOs for canary slice under predicted load profile
Fallback: Automated fallback to compatible model variant occurs <250ms after degraded health signal
Rollback: Automated rollback triggers built and tested (metric thresholds + manual abort) and able to revert to previous model/version within 5 minutes
Observability: Per-route dashboards surfaced in Console with token-level cost, latency, error rates, and quality regressions tied to eval prompts
QA: End-to-end tests (integration + non-regression) passing in staging with synthetic and recorded traffic
Documentation: Customer-facing changelog and migration guidance published and linked from Console
rollout_checklist: Pre-flight: Confirm infra capacity reservations for the expected canary traffic and burst scenarios
Pre-flight: Run eval harness for generation and embeddings; baseline metrics recorded
Pre-flight: Security signoff completed (KMS, audit logs reviewed)
Canary: Start with 0.1% traffic slice for 30 minutes; monitor key metrics
Canary: Expand to 1% for 2 hours if no alert triggers; run synthetic user journeys
Canary: Expand to 5% for 6 hours with automated rollback enabled
Full-roll: Gradual ramp to 100% using doubling windows and watch periods
Post-roll: 24h elevated monitoring window with runbook on-call rotation
launch_readiness: Minimum required: QA green on all acceptance criteria, infra quota confirmed, SRE and on-call rota assigned, telemetry dashboards configured, customer communications drafted, and security/compliance checklist cleared.
post_launch_monitoring: Alerts: p50/p95/p99 latency regressions, error rate spike >0.2% absolute, token cost deviation >15%
Quality alerts: Eval-set drift >5% on key prompts triggers alert to Product and Applied ML
Automated rollback: healthcheck chain reacts to sustained latency or error threshold breaches
SLO reporting: daily digest to owners for first 7 days
Customer signals: Slack channel for support escalations and weekly triage
open_questions: What is the canonical list of eval prompts we must include for embeddings stability?
Do we require tenant-scoped canaries for top 20 customers before general canary?
Who owns final rollback decision for partial rollbacks that affect >=5% traffic?
Should we mandate a staged notification cadence to customers during expanded canaries?
